identity_match.result: matches historical Pacific Hotel south/street facade
evidence: Visible Chinese gold hotel lettering and English PACIFIC HOTEL lettering
Central clock-tower pavilion, gold dome and symmetrical projecting facade wings match textual building description

actually_visible_features.observation: The two outer side pavilions project forward and rise above the recessed central roof line. A much taller central columned clock tower rises above the center. Adjacent modern towers are clearly distinct background buildings.
Warm grey/beige masonry appearance with strong horizontal cornices, block-rusticated vertical piers, repeated narrow dark-framed windows and decorative panels.

Each front wing has three dominant vertical window bays. Its upper cap has a plain top row of three rectangular openings above a columned/recessed window stage. Heavy projecting cornices emphasize the pavilion steps.
actually_visible_features.confidence: high for visible three-bay front wings; depth and exact dimension unmeasured

actually_visible_features.observation: Small projecting balustraded balconies occur high on both side wings and the central facade, with deep supporting brackets.

actually_visible_features.feature: Central roof pavilion below clock tower
actually_visible_features.observation: A raised rectangular center element has an arched central recess/round-headed motif, flanking slender columns and a pronounced cornice; decorative finials flank the tower base.

Two cylindrical/round columned stages are visible. Lower stage has ornate Corinthian-like capitals; upper stage has plainer columns. The clock sits prominently between the stages on the front. A gold rounded dome supports a small reddish lantern and slender finial/spire.
actually_visible_features.confidence: high for arrangement; column-order label tentative

actually_visible_features.observation: Tall rectangular window groups have dark brown/red framing; spandrel inserts look dark and mottled. Upper side caps are simpler and lighter.
actually_visible_features.confidence: high; image color/lighting is not a calibrated material survey

actually_visible_features.observation: Large fluted stone columns are visible below the lower cornice, but most base openings, stairs and pedestrian-level details are covered by trees or outside the clear view.
actually_visible_features.confidence: medium for partial colonnade, low for complete entrance arrangement

assessment_of_parent_model_interpretatio.scope: Excluding the separately described modern north estate block is consistent with a bounded historic-front-building model; this front photograph cannot prove the complete rear boundary.

recommended_recognition_priorities: Preserve two raised projecting side wings, recessed center and dominant central clock tower.
Represent the clock between the columned stages, gold dome and small lantern/finial.
Keep heavy cornices, rusticated piers, three-bay side wings and small balustraded balconies.
Treat lower entrance/stairs and rear geometry as documentary/inferred where this image is occluded.
acceptance: Suitable as a strong primary front-facade visual reference; insufficient by itself for surveyed dimensions, all-around completeness or estate/rear-footprint acceptance.
